llm.summary: This skill appears legitimate for publishing to here.now, but it persists account credentials and enables broad site and Drive management that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Shell, curl, file, jq, and network access are proportionate for uploading sites and Drive files; the scripts include a guard against sending credentials to a non-default base URL unless explicitly overridden.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact includes local helper scripts, but the install/update command uses an unpinned npx source, so future installs may fetch changed code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Most actions are user-directed, but the API key flow tells the agent to save returned credentials immediately, while publishing defaults to live public-link sites unless access controls are set.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes durable credentials to ~/.herenow/credentials and publish state with claim tokens/version data to .herenow/state.json; chmod 600 is protective, but persistent account authority is high impact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Publishing websites and files is coherent with the stated purpose, and Drive support is disclosed in the body, but Drive read/write/export/delete/share-token features and broader account/Site/profile management extend beyond the short publishing-focused description.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable letting the agent upload selected files to here.now, create public or access-controlled live URLs, manage private Drive files, and store a here.now API key on disk for future use. Prefer explicit user confirmation before saving credentials, publishing sensitive content, creating Drive share tokens, using --overwrite, or enabling a non-default base URL.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Drive and workspace capabilities are explicitly described, but they broaden the skill beyond the headline publishing summary, supporting Review rather than a malicious finding.
[AE1] expected: The referenced publish.sh and drive.sh files were present locally and inspected; the partial-inspection scanner concern is not supported by this review.
[LP3] expected: Shell and network use are expected for this helper-script based publishing workflow, though the package lacks a narrow declared permission boundary.
[SQP-1] expected: Activation phrases mostly describe publishing or site sharing; users should still understand that activation can upload content to a live service.
[SQP-2] expected: Live URL creation and public-link default access are disclosed in the skill, but the default visibility is important enough to highlight to users.
[RA2] expected: The observed state files are local publish caches and credential files, not cron jobs, startup hooks, or hidden background persistence.
[RP1] unexpected: The unpinned npx install/update command is a supply-chain risk independent of the publishing purpose.
[EA2] unexpected: The instruction for the agent to save returned API keys immediately without a separate confirmation is the main user-control concern.
[PE2] expected: The cited chmod 600 command is normal file-permission hardening and does not request sudo or root execution.
[E1] expected: External uploads and API calls are central to publishing and Drive storage; the finalize URL and upload URLs come from the service response, so users are relying on the service and base URL guard.
[P4] expected: The instruction not to show .herenow/state.json as a user-facing source of truth is operational guidance, not evidence of hidden behavior.
